description: Tataendy: la llama del fuego. Paraguay arde cada año y la NASA lo registra hace 20 años, pero MODIS y VIIRS no se pueden comparar entre sí. Vamos a armonizarlos en una web pública donde cualquiera vea dónde hay fuego y cómo está el ambiente en su zona.
summary: TATAENDY ("light of fire" in Guaraní) is a web platform that turns two decades of NASA satellite fire data into one clear, comparable monthly calendar for Paraguay. It addresses the challenge of building a harmonized burn-activity calendar: raw MODIS and VIIRS detections are not directly comparable, so we aggregate them to a common "active cell-day" grid and apply a calibrated factor (k) to merge MODIS (2001-2011) and VIIRS (2012-present) into a single consistent series, with out-of-sample validation. The app lets anyone explore an interactive map by department, a fire calendar revealing seasonality, anomaly detection versus the historical median, a live 48-hour view, data downloads (Excel/CSV/PNG/JSON), a printable report, email alerts, and a training game. This matters because Paraguay faces intensifying wildfires: a free, transparent, 20-year view helps communities and institutions anticipate, compare and respond faster. Interface available in Spanish and English.
details:
WHAT IT DOES / HOW IT WORKS

TATAENDY harmonizes NASA's MODIS and VIIRS active-fire detections into a single, comparable monthly "fire calendar" for Paraguay (2001-present). Raw MODIS and VIIRS data are not directly comparable (different resolution and number of daily passes), so each hotspot is assigned to a common 0.01 degree "active cell-day" grid, counted once per sensor per day. During the sensor overlap we estimate a per-tile calibration factor k = VIIRS/MODIS (shrunk toward a global value when data are sparse) and scale MODIS to the VIIRS reference, producing one consistent series. The result is validated out-of-sample (the factor is fit on the first half of the overlap and tested on the second). A Python backend serves the harmonized data to an interactive web app.

BENEFITS AND EXPECTED IMPACT

Paraguay faces recurring, intensifying wildfires, but fire information is fragmented across satellites and formats. TATAENDY gives firefighters, emergency staff, scientists and land managers a free, transparent, 20-year view: an interactive map by department, a seasonality calendar, anomaly detection versus the historical median, a current-month alert, a live 48-hour view, one-click downloads (colored Excel, CSV, PNG, JSON), a printable PDF report, NASA FIRMS email-alert setup, and a training game on how to respond to fires. This helps communities anticipate the fire season, compare the present against history, and act in time.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES AND SOFTWARE

Backend: Python (standard library only, no heavy dependencies) with a SQLite database built by an automated data pipeline. Frontend: vanilla JavaScript, HTML and CSS with the Leaflet mapping library. Data: NASA FIRMS (MODIS C6.1 and VIIRS 375 m). Administrative boundaries from geoBoundaries; base map from Esri. The whole project is lightweight, reproducible and easy to run anywhere.

CREATIVITY

Instead of showing raw, incomparable satellite counts, we solve the scientific comparability problem with a calibrated, validated harmonization and present it as an intuitive "fire calendar" that non-experts can read at a glance. We added a safety training game and a bilingual (Spanish/English) interface to make the data genuinely useful to the public.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Accuracy (out-of-sample validation and transparency panels), accessibility (colorblind-safe color ramps, light/dark mode, mobile-friendly, two languages), honesty about limitations (e.g., Terra-only years before 2002), and real-world usefulness (email alerts that keep working outside the app, and downloadable data for further analysis).
